query: For AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock intended for additively manufactured miniature components, what single intervention could overcome the residual thermal stresses, degraded mechanical properties, and processing complexity associated with mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing regimes? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions, states the applicable processing window, geometry, and test conditions, identifies supporting prior evidence, and describes a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Implementing an in-situ, low‐temperature post‐build annealing treatment immediately after laser powder bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock will relax residual thermal stresses, enable a controlled evolution of the microstructure (by reducing high-density dislocation networks and promoting a beneficial fine-phase distribution), and thus restore or enhance the mechanical properties while simplifying the processing complexity compared to conventional high-thermal-load regimes.
generation.material_initial_state: As-built miniature components made from AlCrFeNiSi processed under standard high-thermal-load LPBF conditions exhibiting high residual stresses, a non-equilibrium microstructure (e.g., excessive dislocation density and possible undesirable phase formation), and compromised mechanical behavior.
generation.intervention: Apply an in-situ, rapid low-temperature (≈700 °C or below) annealing treatment immediately following deposition within the build chamber.
generation.conditions: The treatment is conducted under an inert atmosphere immediately post-build on miniature components to allow stress relief without significant grain growth, followed by standard mechanical (tensile, hardness) and microstructural (SEM, EBSD) evaluations.
generation.structural_mediator: Relaxation of dense dislocation networks and stabilization of fine eutectic or precipitate phases that distribute load more uniformly.
generation.mechanism: The controlled annealing cycle affords limited atomic diffusion that relieves internal stresses by reducing dislocation crowding and suppressing formation of detrimental nonequilibrium phases. This controlled heat treatment leads to a more homogeneous and stable microstructure, thereby improving mechanical properties without the need for extensive high-energy processing adjustments.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to conventional high-thermal-load LPBF parts, the annealed components should exhibit significantly lower residual stresses, improved yield strength and ductility, and a more manageable processing window for additive manufacturing of miniature components.
generation.baseline: Conventional LPBF processing of AlCrFeNiSi feedstock at high thermal loads yields parts with elevated residual stresses, degraded mechanical properties, and increased complexity in process optimization.
generation.boundary: The annealing temperature should not exceed about 700 °C and the exposure time must be controlled to avoid excessive grain growth or coarsening. The optimal thermal window may vary with component size, geometry, and the influence of Si on diffusion kinetics.
generation.uncertainty: Precise temperature and duration settings for conformal annealing, as well as potential compositional influences from Si on the stress-relief kinetics and phase evolution, require further experimental calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of AlCrFeNiSi miniature components via LPBF under identical conditions. Immediately after printing, subject one set to the proposed low-temperature (≈700 °C) in-situ annealing treatment for a pre-defined short duration, while leaving the other set as a control. Evaluate both groups using X-ray diffraction (for residual stress), SEM/EBSD (for microstructure and grain size), and mechanical testing (tensile strength, yield strength, ductility, hardness).
measurements: Dislocation density and phase distribution via SEM/EBSD
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed components do not show a statistically significant reduction in residual stresses and meaningful improvement in mechanical properties (or if detrimental microstructural changes occur) compared to the untreated control, this would falsify the hypothesis.

Synergistic Strength–Ductility Improvement in an Additively Manufactured Body-Centered Cubic HfNbTaTiZr High-Entropy Alloy via Deep Cryogenic Treatment

Abstract: AbstractHfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy has wide application prospects as a biomedical material, and the use of laser additive manufacturing can solve the forming problems faced by the alloy. In view of the characteristics of the one-time forming of additive manufacturing methods, it is necessary to develop non-mechanical processing modification methods. In this paper, deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) is first applied to the modification of a HEA with BCC structure, then the post-processing method of DCT is combined with laser melting deposition (LMD) technology to successfully realize the coordinated improvement of forming and strength–ductility synergistic improvement in lightweight Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr alloy. The final tensile strength of the alloy after DCT treatment is 25% higher than that of the as-cast alloy and 11% higher than that of the as-deposited alloy, and the elongation is increased by 48% and 10%, respectively. In addition, DCT also achieves induced phase transition without additional deformation.Keywords: laser

Investigation of the Microstructural Evolution and Mechanical Properties of the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA Fabricated by Additive Manufacturing Assisted by Heat Treatment

Abstract: Eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs) exhibit excellent casting properties and comprehensive mechanical performance, making them suitable for fabricating spatial engineering components using additive manufacturing techniques. However, the rapid solidification process also leads to increased internal stress and reduced structural stability in the components. Therefore, this study focuses on the AlFeCoCrNi2.1 EHEA as the research subject, utilizing laser additive manufacturing to fabricate components and systematically investigating the influence of heat treatment processes on the microstructure and mechanical properties of the components. The research demonstrates that low-temperature heat treatment (700 °C and below) acts as a stress relief-annealing process for the components. The yield strength decreased from 1003.2 MPa to 742.1 MPa.
